scenes.headline: How to read a quant's bit allocation from its header
scenes.sub: Penjing-27B's measured-allocation claim, checked against the GGUF tensor table.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Turbo! These low-bit quants claim their bits were placed by measurement. Here's how, and what the files show.

scenes.label: Measured allocation
scenes.text: Measure which tensor groups matter by crushing each one in turn and watching KL, then place bits to fit the target machine's memory.
scenes.say: Measure which parts matter by crushing each one in turn, then spend a memory budget where it counts.

items.text: Crush one tensor group at a time
items.say: Crush one group of tensors at a time, and measure its KL divergence from full precision, against the model's own noise curve.

items.text: Fit bits to a memory budget
items.say: Then allocate bits to minimise KL within the target machine's memory.

items.text: Every tensor's type lands in the header
items.say: Each tensor's type is written in the header, readable without the weights.

scenes.title: What the headers show, block by block

steps.label: IQ3_S file: one type in every block
steps.say: In the largest file, every block gets the same type. No per-layer structure.

steps.label: Blocks 0, 1, 63, 64 kept; 2 to 62 crushed
steps.say: In the three smaller files, blocks zero, one, sixty-three and sixty-four keep the primary type. Blocks two to sixty-two crush their gate and up weights.

steps.label: A fixed rule, not a per-budget knapsack
steps.note: the same keep-set at 1.91, 2.12 and 2.15 bpw
steps.say: Same keep-set at three budgets. A knapsack re-solved per budget would not normally do that; a first-and-last rule would.

left.title: Demote attention K and V
items: Saves 11 MB of a 7.34 GB file
The most sensitive tensors in the stack
left.say: Demoting attention keys and values saves eleven megabytes of seven point three four gigabytes, from the most sensitive tensors.

right.title: Demote FFN gate and up
right.say: Demoting the feed-forward gate and up saves seven hundred and sixty-five megabytes. That's the real lever.

scenes.label: measured bits per weight, in the file whose name says 1.75
scenes.note: the LM head alone is 13.4% of the file, at Q5_K
scenes.say: No file weighs what its name says. The one named one point seven five measures one point nine oh six: its output head alone is thirteen point four percent.

scenes.text: The filename is marketing; the tensor-info block at the top of the file is the build.

recap: Crush each group, measure KL, fit a budget
The bytes sit in FFN gate, up and LM head
scenes.say: To recap: measure, fit, and then check the header, because the header is the build.
